fichas.title: Laboratories: workstation clearances and planning
fichas.summary: Laboratories are classified by use and subject. Tuition-related practical laboratories accommodate many workstations with basic equipment; research laboratories are generally smaller and include specialized equipment and ancillary rooms. Chemistry and biology laboratories typically have fixed benches, high air exchange and sometimes fume cupboards; physics laboratories often have mobile benches and electrical services in wall ducts or suspended from the ceiling. Clean rooms use filtered air and controlled circulation.

fichas.title: Clean-room laboratory and laboratory safety levels
fichas.summary: Clean-room laboratories provide dust-free filtered air for work such as microelectronics and for hazardous substances that must be prevented from spreading to adjoining rooms. The illustrated examples identify level 3 and level 4 safety provisions, including safety lobbies, protective clothing, disinfection, controlled access, specialized workbenches, autoclaves and ventilation and environmental-control systems. A note states that certain level 4 provisions are required only when upgrading to a level 4 laboratory.
